Why did my old Volkswagon Quantum have 5 cylinders instead of 4 or 6?

This is a tricky and complicated question that it's hard to explain to someone without basic knowledge of how an internal combustion engine works, so for the purpose of this answer I will assume that you have this basic knowledge (Feel free to ask away if you miss something)

A 4 cylinder engine only makes power every 180 Deg rotation of the crankshaft, this means that the power stroke won't overlap.

https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/d/dc/4StrokeEngine_Ortho_3D_Small.gif

On a 5 Cylinder engine however there is one more cylinder, so 720 (360*2 since in a 4 stroke it takes two spins of the crank to make power) ... 720/5 is 144. Since each power stroke lasts for 180 Deg this basically means that the power strokes overlap so the engine is always in "power mode"

http://www.makingdifferent.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/06/4-strokes-of-engine-1.gif

While this has advantages (Runs smoother and has better torque delivery) it also has several cons (an uneven number of cylinders means that the crank is not perfectly balanced and so there is vibrations at high RPMs)

Additionally I suggest watching this video form one of my favorite channels "Engineering explained" To better understand the number of cylinders and crankshaft angle relationship

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aonbwOxooGA

EDIT: Jason is the MAN! He actually has a very detailed video explaining this in DETAIL ... here ya go https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VBUyR7xQvhY
